en: The Great Compassionate and Merciful Dharani of the Heart of the Blue-Necked One,
the Sovereign King Avalokitesvara Who Saves from Suffering, Vast, Perfect, Unobstructed, and Sovereign.

Translated by the Great One of Vast Wisdom, Amoghavajra: Homage, refuge, and prostrations to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Teacher of the True Dharma, in the Pure Land of Potalaka upon the southern ocean.
Avalokiteśvara’s original teacher is Amitāyus Tathāgata;
Avalokiteśvara’s original and true teacher is Prabhāpāla Tathāgata.
Homage to the Great Dhāraṇī of the Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Great Compassionate Heart of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The Dharani for Saving from Suffering;
the Dharani for Extending Life;
and the Dharani for Increasing the Elimination of Evil Destinies.
The Dharani for Destroying Karmic Obstructions, the Dharani for Fulfilling Vows,
the Dharani for Sovereignty According to One's Mind,
and the Dharani for Swiftly Transcending the Higher Stages.
The Dharani for Transcending the Eighth Stage upon Hearing It Once;
the Dharani for the Simultaneous Elimination of the Four Hundred and Four Diseases.
*Namaḥ ratnatrayāya*. This is the original form of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
One should exercise great compassion and refrain from speaking loudly, lest the nature of this deity be suddenly disturbed.
Nama ārya: these two syllables are the essential body of the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra.
Recite this while keeping it in mind:
*Vairocana*. This is the Vairocanapāṇy-avalokiteśvara.
In the past, the Bodhisattva recited this principle to transform [sentient beings].
*Bodhisattvānām* (Buddha-sattva-ta-bhyo): this is the mantra of the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa, who subdues the hosts of celestial armies.
*Mahāsattvānām* (Ma-ha-sattva-bhyo): this is the causal seed-syllable of that Bodhisattva.
Recite the mantra of the principal deity:
*ma-ha-ka-la-ni-ka-rya*. This is the essential form of Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa.
The Bodhisattva’s own body holds the *vajra* mudrā in his hand.
Oṃ. This is the divine speech of Oṃ.
All should join their palms and listen as the mantra is recited:
Saptāra-pāy-e. These are the actual forms of the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
Subduing the Māra King.
*Śū* *tana* *tatsya*. (9) These are the names of the Four Great Heavenly Kings and the eight classes of spirits and deities.
*Namaḥ samantavate i maṃ ariye*. (10) This is the original form of the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.
One must recite this with focused attention and not allow it to become lax;
do not let the nature of the Bodhisattva Saṃbhava be neglected. *Bha-lu-ki-ti-śi-bu-laṃ-da-ba*. (11) This is the original body of our Teacher, Vairocana Buddha.
Vast, Perfect, and Inconceivable Merit.
*Namaḥ* (Nanmo) *Amitābha* (Wunuo Ralengzhai). This is the original body of the Pure and Perfect Reward Body Buddha, Vairocana.
You must apply your mind and not be negligent.
*He* *Li* *Ma* *Bo* *Da* *Sha* *Mei*. Thirteen. This is the King of the Half-Headed Spirits (*Ardhakapāla*).
Kukdamo takes them as his retinue.
*Svādhatuṣpaṃ*. (14) These are the clansmen of the Bodhisattva Amṛta, who is also the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
He takes them as his retinue.
*Ā* (阿), *yū* (遊), *yìng* (孕)— these fifteen [syllables] constitute the Great King of the Flying Yakṣas,
who patrols the four quarters to examine right and wrong.
16. *Svabhāvatnamo vākya*. This is the King of the Bhūtas; his form is black and large.
He wears a leopard skin as his garment.
The deity holds a garment and a trident in his hands.
*Ma-pa-ta-du* (17). This is the original form of the Kṣatriya Bodhisattva.
He is the one with an iron wheel in hand, holding a yakṣa-sūtra, and possessing three eyes.
Tadyathā (18) Oṃ. This is the mantra of the sword.
Āḥ Parolokāgati (19). This was spoken by the Brahmā King himself; the Buddha is the family (kula).
*Ka-ra-te* (20): These are the five deities who establish the gates;
they are tall and black in color.
*I-hri-li* (21): This is the King of the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
This is the divine King Maheśvara leading the celestial armies.
*Maha-bodhisattva* (22): this is the Jewel-mind (*ratnacitta*), free from any distracted or confused mind; the term *sattva* refers to this state.
23. *Sarvasarva*. This is the Bodhisattva Gandhavyūha (Fragrant Accumulation).
He commands the military forces of the five directions, with *sarva* as his attendants; he is inconceivable.
MĀ RĀ MĀRĀ MĀ MA HṚDA YA (24, same as above) KURU KURU KA CAM (25). This is the Emptiness-Body Bodhisattva.
The General Who Subdues Husbands leads twenty trillion celestial armies.
*Du lo du lo pa ja ye ti*. This is the Bodhisattva Yaṅjun (Yanjun).
The Army of the Peacock King:
*Mahāvajraśāye* (27, same as above) *Dhara-dhara* (28). This is Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Holding a large handle of the golden wheel.
*Dhāriṇī* (29). This is the Lion King;
his army is invincible and cannot be subdued.
*Rā* (30) is the thunderbolt that subdues the retinue of Māras.
*Ccha-ra* (31), *ccha-ra*—this is the one who shatters the Bodhisattvas.
The principal deity himself holds a golden wheel in his hand.
*Ma ma* [the disciple] so-and-so, receive and uphold this. *Vajra-māra*, thirty-two times; this is the great subduing-māra vajra of the principal deity.
Holding a golden wheel in his hand.
Mu-di-shai (Mudrā-śrī). Thirty-three [devas]. This is the Buddha’s gesture of joined palms.
Listen as I recite the wondrous verses of the good deity, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes.
I-he-i-he (34): This is the invocation of the deity Maheśvara.
Ś-na-ś-na (35): As above. A-ra-saṃ-bu-ra-śa-li (36): This is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Holding a military bow and arrow in hand.
Vaṃ phaṭ | Saṃ phaṭ | Bhañja bhañja śāmya. (37) This is the original body of Amitābha Buddha.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Master:
Hūḥ, hulu, hūḥ, hulu, ma, ra. (38) These are the invocations of the eight classes of spirits and deities.
Hū (39) as above; Śara (40). This refers to the world of the five turbidities (*pañcakaṣāya*).
Sī sī (41); Sū rū sū rū (42). These are the sounds of the trees of bliss belonging to all the Buddhas.
43. *Bodhiye bodhiye*. This is Avalokiteśvara’s [mantra] for anticipating the evils of sentient beings.
44. *Bodhaye bodhaye*. This is the original essence of Ānanda.
Mi-ti-li-ye (45). This is the Bodhisattva Maitreya holding a golden knife in his hand.
Na-ra-ge-ni-chi (46). This is the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.
Holding a long golden sword in his hand:
*Tāriṣeṇa-naparya-mana* (47). This is the Bodhisattva Golden Light Banner (*Suvarṇaketu*).
Holding a vajra scepter in hand:
*Svāhā* (48). The above is the same. *Siddhya* (49). This is the gateway to penetrating all dharmas.
*Svāhā* (50). These are the fifty dharmic words. *Mahoṣṭhitāya svāhā*. This is the banner held in the hand of the Bodhisattva Prabhāketudhvaja.
SIDDHYE (52): This is the Great Bodhisattva Devasya; he comes holding a sword in his hand, or the Bodhisattva holds a water bowl in his hand.
Śivā-gara-ye svāhā (53). This is called the Anśitakṣa incense.
Nara-kīrti (55), as above, svāhā (56). Māra-nara (57). This is the Bodhisattva Sannodaka holding a water bowl in his hand.
*Svāhā* (58, same as above). *Sira-saṃ-ā-muk-khaya* (59). This is the mantra of the Bodhisattva Sāgaradatta, who holds a golden hook in his hand.
Svāhā (60). Same as above. Bha-ma-ha-si-ta-ya (61). Same as above. Svāhā (62). Same as above. Jva-la-gi-ra-a-si-ta-ya (63). This is the practice of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja himself against Māra.
*Svāhā* (64, same as above). *Bhagavac-chāstṛ-nātha* (65). This is the practice of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja in his previous life when he was afflicted by Māra’s pain.
Svāhā (66) [same as above]; Nara-kañcī-pā-kara-rātrayaḥ (67) [same as above];
Svāhā (68) [same as above]; Mā-vā-ri-śreṣṭha-karman-rātraḥ (69) [same as above]; Svāhā.
Vahana-mukhara-tantra-tāraya nama amṛte varajite śobhara-ya bodhi.
Ti-sa-po-ha. One fascicle of the Dharani of Avalokiteśvara with the Blue Neck. For the mudrā of the Great Compassionate Heart of the Blue-necked One:
join the palms with hollowed fingers and bend the two index fingers.

The second joints of both thumbs are the conch; the two middle fingers joined vertically are the lotus; the two ring fingers joined vertically and rounded at the tips are the wheel; and the two little fingers joined straight upward are the staff. Thus, these four seals are complete within a single mudrā.
That is to say, the conch, the lotus, the wheel, and the staff.
